USELESS app. This is the most useless app I’ve ever had the displeasure of using. I don’t know anyone who’s ever gotten a job from Handshake; using LinkedIn or even just periodically checking your target companies’ Careers webpages will be a more effective way to discover and apply for opportunities. Anything that can be found on Handshake can be found in either of those places presented in a much nicer format, and surrounded by much fewer scam job postings. Additionally, the feed “feature” that Handshake added in an attempt to make their app scroll-worthy only feels depressing because EVERY SINGLE POST is just other unemployed people asking “so how do I get a job? Do you have a job for me? Does anyone have any tips?” Employers don’t post on Handshake because who on Earth cares about posting on Handshake. They have better things to do. All of the posts are from the other young grads you’re competing with, which really just helps you grasp how bleak the job market is. And it doesn’t even show you posts from people relevant to you; I’ve NEVER seen a Handshake post from someone even in my state, much less at my specific university. It’s all a bunch of randos from Florida and Texas, people who I’m sure are great but are very distant from where I am. If you want the job search to feel statistically hopeless and logistically convoluted, use Handshake. If you want a good experience, use literally any other app.

This app isn't developed well for mobile devices. Tap in a search field and your keyboard comes up. Minimize your keyboard and the search feature goes away. Try again, type and search. You can only see the first five results as your keyboard covers the rest of the results. Minimize your keyboard and the search results disappear. Plus the popups asking you to turn on notifications is overkill. No means No.

I don't think this is the safest app for searching for a job. Maybe for internships, and it has a lot of listings that are actually entry level (something hard to find on job sites like Indeed/LinkedIn). I'm not sure what, if any, screening jobs go through on this site, but every single "employer" that has contacted me regarding an application has been a job scam.

There's seemingly no way to adjust the distance of jobs you get recommended despite the ability to list preferred locations on your profile so I always get notifs about onsite jobs on the opposite side of the country even though I don't plan on leaving the state. The amount of AI related job listings and constant recruiter messages/emails asking if you would be interested in training Handshake's AI is really obnoxious and it seems like there's no way to block or filter out these offers either.

i have been experiencing a possible bug witb this app for quite a while now. i cannot open messages in my inbox. it doesnt even register that im tapping on the message to open it. its literally this most important feature, and it doesnt work. the inbox loads messages fine and shows the preview, but no matter what i do i cannot open any messages, i click everywhere and nothing happens.

I have never gotten a job with Handshake. There are a lot of employers on this app looking to waste peoples' time. It can sometimes take upwards of 30 minutes to a few hours applying for jobs for each posting, and it has never been fruitful for me. All of that time spent on applications is exhausting, energy draining and time consuming, and it is all unpaid. Despite my impressive work experience and educational background, many and most of my applications get rejected quickly.

Because you can't set job preferences for on-site or remote, and aren't matched by your actual resume skills or degrees, I often get "matched" or messaged by recruiters for jobs I can't apply to. They're either on-site and half a country away, or require degrees I don't have. Most of the recruiters are just copy pasting messages anyway and not actually engaging. So, this platform has not been very useful for my job search, and I'm very disappointed in it.

Good app, shows jobs in my area and much further, even when you enter in your mile range you'd like to stay within. Making things a little easier to navigate would be nice, such as being taken straight to the job post when I receive the "new job listing" update in my email. Instead, I have to go searching for it on my own and I don't always find it. Otherwise it's a good and helpful app.

It's a slightly simpler LinkedIn parallel app, usable for students. I don't think most of the opportunities that are coming up are in my field, so I have to search. I definitely want to say that the ability to *block* specific keywords would be really nice, or block specific messages to my inbox. (I want to block anything that has AI involved, and I keep getting emails from the same two companies after saying I'm not interested, and they're not even my field) 3/5: Works, but not helpful so far

Wouldn't let me edit my profile! It let me open my profile, click the edit button, click the text box, my keyboard auto opens, but then nothing happens when I type or try to edit in any way. If I can't do even the simplest of things, I'm not sure how the app is supposed to be useful at all. Seems completely broken. I tried again after the latest update and it's still broken.

The app has a great design and offers many job opportunities. However, I have yet to receive any responses from employers. As an Information Technology student, I keep getting job offers for teaching, military, and law enforcement positions, which are unrelated to my field. Recruiters should be more attentive when reaching out to students to ensure the opportunities align with their qualifications and career goals.

You can't set parameters for distance from a particular location in your filters. On the website I could go within 5 miles, 15 Mile, 20 miles Etc. It is extremely bothersome that I cannot do this on the app, this is a very small implementation and should be completed immediately. I have to scroll through a thousand jobs instead of a hundred due to this. Huge waste of time.

If you favorite a job, you'll never see it / find it again until it's about to expire. You would think that'd be one of the easiest things to find. The jobs recommended rarely have anything to do with my interests, education, or location. The emails I get with new/expiring jobs link to my browser and not to the app. The last two emails I've recieved, I've searched for the job and the app can't find it. Now, I can't log in. It only wants a temp passcode that it won't send, not my password?

This app is basically spam/harassment. I set the job notification parameters to only be to 3 locations, but I get a notification for EVERY SINGLE job in my field no matter where it is. It's at least 10 notifications a day. When emailing support, they told me to adjust my notifications (already had, doesn't work) or to turn off messages from employers (never been a problem). It's absurd for me to be notified of every job posting on the opposite side of country when I'm not relocating.

I wish there was a way to filter out messages we don't want. I filled out my job and location preferences and all I get are messages about jobs that are too far away or in an industry I have no interest in. Employers pay zero attention! They pick who to message based on major and that's it. I'm assuming it's just mass messaging and the person on the other end isn't actually reviewing profiles and preferences. I get a lot of messages, all irrelevant, so it's annoying.

Most of the messages and notifications I get are completely irrelevant to me. I've tried to adjust things by editing my profile and such, but there doesn't seem to be any sort of algorithm or targeted recommendations. The job board and search functionality is unsophisticated and frequently advertises jobs that were filled months or years ago.

You can apply to countless jobs but options are limited as this app is only but so widely used. Solicitation is common especially for teaching positions and "no degree needed" positions. There needs to be a more verifiable way for recruiters to only solicit actually relevant majors. I am in physical science and have had countless sales, real estate, finance, and irrelevant teaching positions pushed on me. There needs to be a way to report spam from them

Want to get $35,000/yr for a sales job? If no, then don't bother with this app. I have a full profile with my degrees and preferences set, but I still get 2+ messages each day from recruiters for sales positions. The messages are annoying ,especially because my profile indicates no desire to move to AZ for sales (which is not one of my interests). I have yet to have a meaningful conversation with people in my field.

Seems like it would be helpful - If only it was accurate. When I connected from my school, it incorrectly listed my major & I couldn't find how to change that at first. When I finally figured it out (Or so I thought), I kept getting messages from perhaps well-meaning recruiter accounts; however, they are recounting inaccurate information about me that I'm guessing they are seeing from my profile, including location & job goals. The concept seems nice but these inaccuracies are very frustrating.

Hasn't recommended me a job/internship even remotely related to my major, sets my class to sophomore every time I try to set it to freshman, and doesn't even show applicable jobs/internships no matter how many filters I set. I don't understand what the point of this app is if I have to manually scroll through listings, can't upload a resume, and it doesn't show the requirements for the listing unless I spend a minute or 2 scrolling through the description. A waste of time.

Most of the recruiters out there are bots. They send you automated messages and pretend to have read your resume, and don't respond to your messages back. It is very difficult to report an agency, and the one time I did nothing was resolved. There is no way to block people on this app, so I am getting spammed from 'recruiters' for jobs I am not interested in. The only reason I got this app in the first place was because my college's career services recommended it...

I know it most likely won't make a difference as you have many people on this app but I feel like this hasn't been helpful at all in gaining employment. Not helpful for someone with many years of experience in my field that decided to pursue a goal of obtaining my degree. I find that about eight out of ten offers are for internships which is something I'm not interested in. A lot of spam when recruiters don't answer you yet they send you offers.

UI looks good, and the service is helpful but other parts stink. It doesn't give helpful notifications. The most I see is apply to jobs expiring soon, but it doesn't mention which jobs those are nor how long. And when you check in the app, theres no easy way to see the date without clicking on the job. The most frustrating thing is not seeing jobs I've liked. Might've missed it, but I've looked. Only feeds like jobs in research or finance, not one of the actual jobs I've said I'm interested in.

My experience with this app is through two colleges, as both a student and as a staff member and in both situations I would sum this up as an entirely gimmick-based LinkedIn alternative. Most college administration's are partnering and pushing this app heavily, and other than marketing internship webinars, and a lot of advertising of unavailable jobs, I have yet to meet any student who has gotten anything meaningful from the app. The app partners with college career advisors, in a generic form.

They had a server error that failed to forward days worth of job applications to the respective employer, then had the audacity to email me a separate time for each job like "don't worry you still have 3 days to apply!" WHAT? I filled these out in December and you wait until late February to tell me you didn't send them? Now of course I am back in class, and no longer on break, so I don't have time to re-apply to all of these places. Handshake very well may have cost me an internship. Dont use.

Great app but all features aren't working as designed. I'm receiving tons of emails from recruiters but when I check the Handshake app for the messages they don't appear. Because of this I am unable to respond to the messages and may be missing out on great opportunities. I would have given a 5 star rating if mt inbox actually received the messages.

Simple yet frustrating, apply to positions are quick and oftentimes painless. However, the job boards aren't updated so many of the opportunities have either already been filled or aren't being considered anymore. Having a large number of applications accidently go through for a position that's been filled already isn't just a waste of time but also a bit embarrassing.

When I click on email links, the app opens first in my browser with a big overlay that gives me a button to open in the app. I can't view any of the information in the browser because of that. Upon clicking to open the information in the app, it opens handshake on a default start page and does not take me to the relevant information from the link.

The search functionality doesn't work very well. Most employers are looking for interns and hiring out into the future. Limited prospects if you need a job this year and don't already have a degree. There's a lot of seemingly fake AI spam jobs. Messages don't open on mobile. The app overall is ok, but it's basically a LinkedIn clone for students.

This is a great app with a great UI, but the whole thing is just for companies to message college students about underpaid internships, spam you with messages for career events, and never follow up with prospects. Schools wasting their money on this program would be better off creating a SharePoint to house information. Its a shame because it has so much potential, but it's wasted.

Just something I added because of school. Not sure if it is good or not because I barely use it. (Maybe like once a year.) If it gave better suggestions or had a more variety of employers I might use it. Right now the app doesn't offer any suggestions for jobs that are in the field of Physics, which I am going to school for.
